changes.text: 魏国公子（下称公子）的姐姐，是赵国平原君（赵惠文王之弟）的夫人。魏安釐王二十年，秦军击破赵长平军之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵。秦王遣使警告魏王：攻赵旦暮可下，诸侯有敢救赵的，拔赵之后必先移兵击之。魏王恐惧，派人叫晋鄙停军，驻扎在邺，「名為救趙，實持兩端以觀望」。平原君的使者冠盖相属，赶到魏国，责让公子：平原君说，自己之所以与公子结为婚姻，是看重公子的高义，以为公子能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国的救兵至今不到，公子能急人之困又在哪里？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。难处在于：救兵听命于魏王，而魏王畏秦，按兵不动。

The Wei prince's elder sister was the wife of Lord Pingyuan of Zhao (younger brother of King Huiwen of Zhao). In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had broken Zhao's army at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao. The king of Qin sent an envoy to warn the king of Wei that Zhao would fall any day, and that whichever of the lords dared to relieve it, Qin would turn its troops on first once Zhao was taken. The king of Wei, afraid, sent orders halting Jin Bi, who encamped at Ye — nominally relieving Zhao, in fact keeping a foot in both camps and waiting to see. Lord Pingyuan's envoys arrived in Wei one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — reproaching the prince: Lord Pingyuan said he had joined himself to the prince by marriage because he valued the prince's high sense of duty and believed him a man who would rush to others in distress; now Handan was within days of surrendering to Qin, and Wei's relief still had not come — where, then, was that readiness to rush to others in distress? They added, in translation: had he no pity for his own sister? The difficulty: the relief army answered to the king of Wei, and the king, fearing Qin, kept it standing still.
侯生给出的方案：他说，他听闻晋鄙的兵符常在魏王卧内，如姬最幸，出入卧内，有办法窃取。他又说，他听闻如姬的父亲被人所杀，三年未能报仇，自王以下想替她报父仇的都没能做到；她曾向公子泣诉，公子使客斩了仇人的头敬献给她。侯生说如姬「欲為公子死，無所辭，顧未有路耳」，所以公子开口请她，她必许。得虎符、夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。公子从其计，去请如姬，「如姬果盜晉鄙兵符與公子」。

Hou Ying's plan, as he laid it out: he said he had heard that Jin Bi's army tally — a tiger tally — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber, and that Lady Ruji, the king's favorite, came and went there and was able to steal it. He went on: he had also heard that her father had been murdered; for three years she had sought revenge, and no one, from the king down, had been able to avenge him. She had wept to the prince, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and presented it to her respectfully. Hou Ying said she was ready to die for the prince and would refuse him nothing; only, in translation, she had not yet had the opportunity. If the prince would but ask, she would certainly agree. Then, with the tiger tally in hand, he could seize Jin Bi's army, relieve Zhao in the north and drive Qin back in the west — in translation, an achievement to rank with the Five Hegemons. The prince followed the plan and asked Lady Ruji; she did indeed steal Jin Bi's army tally and give it to him.
魏王怒公子盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，公子自己清楚。原文紧接着记：退秦存赵之后，他派将领率军归魏，自己与门客留在赵国。这场救赵中盗符夺军、矫杀晋鄙的一段没有魏王的授权。

The king of Wei was furious that the prince had stolen his tally and killed Jin Bi on a forged order, and the prince knew it. The source goes on directly: having driven off Qin and saved Zhao, he had a general lead the army back to Wei and stayed behind in Zhao with his retainers. The part of the rescue of Zhao in which he stole the tally, seized the army and killed Jin Bi carried no royal authorization.

第三处是事后的账。门客那句「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」把两边算清：功劳是赵国的，亏欠是魏国的。原文记他受劝后立即自责，又在赵王面前侧行辞让，自言负魏、无功于赵，赵王因此终未献五城。至于留赵，原文把它紧接在魏王之怒与「公子亦自知也」之后；后文又记他「留趙十年不歸」，魏王派使者来请时，他「恐其怒之」，告诫门下敢替魏王使者通报者死；直到毛公、薛公往见，责他魏急而不恤，他才「立變色，告車趣駕歸救魏」，魏王见到他，两人相对而泣，魏王授他上将军印。事情并没有停在这里：秦王行金万斤于魏，求晋鄙的门客在魏王面前毁谤公子；魏王日闻其毁，不能不信，后来果然使人代公子将；公子自知再以毁废，谢病不朝，与宾客长夜饮，日夜为乐饮者四岁，「竟病酒而卒」。作者的一种解释是，秦国专找「晉鄙客」来毁谤，矫杀晋鄙这笔账最终也落回到他自己身上；原文并未明说两者之间的关联。至于留赵，一种解释是，他以留在赵国、不回魏国的方式认下了这笔债；但照原文，留赵也可能出于躲避魏王之怒，这一解读只能存疑。作者认为，他真正把这笔债说出口，是辞让五城时自言负魏的那一刻。

The third is the accounting afterward. The retainer's words — in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — keep both columns straight: the credit belongs to Zhao, the debt to Wei. The source records that he blamed himself at once when rebuked, and that before the king of Zhao he stepped aside and declined, saying he had wronged Wei and had no merit in Zhao, so that the king never offered the five cities. As for staying in Zhao, the source places it directly after the king of Wei's anger and the note that the prince knew of it; later it records that he stayed in Zhao for ten years without returning, and that when the king of Wei sent envoys to ask for him, he feared the king's anger and warned his household that anyone who passed on a message from the king's envoys would die. Only when Mao Gong and Xue Gong went to see him and rebuked him for ignoring Wei in its peril did he, in translation, change countenance at once and order his carriage readied to go home and save Wei; on seeing him, the king of Wei wept with him and gave him the seal of supreme general. The story does not end there: the king of Qin spent ten thousand jin of gold in Wei, seeking out Jin Bi's former retainers to slander the prince to the king of Wei; hearing the slander daily, the king could not help believing it, and in the end had someone else replace the prince in command; knowing he had been cast aside by slander a second time, the prince pleaded illness and stayed away from court, drinking through the nights with his guests, carousing day and night for four years, until, in translation, he finally died of drink. One reading the author offers is that by Qin's seeking out Jin Bi's own retainers to do the slandering, the account of killing Jin Bi on a forged order came back to rest on the prince himself; the source does not state any such connection. As for staying in Zhao, one reading is that he acknowledged the debt by staying there rather than returning to Wei; but on the source's own account, staying in Zhao may equally have been a way of avoiding the king's anger, so that reading must remain tentative. In the author's view, the moment he actually spoke the debt aloud was when he declined the five cities and admitted he had wronged Wei.
第二处是把坏情况写进计划。侯生提醒将在外、主令有所不受，于是朱亥随行、袖中藏椎，晋鄙听则已，不听则击。作者推断，这一步的难处不在敢不敢：公子听后的反应是流泪说，怕晋鄙不听，到时必须杀他，自己并非怕死。作者认为，从结果看，他欠了自己这方一笔债——杀本国宿将、盗王符、惹魏王怒——仍然把方案走完。原文记他事前已料到晋鄙恐不听、必当杀之；至于盗符、惹魏王怒等其他代价，原文没有写他事前是否掂量过。

The second undignified spot is writing the bad case into the plan. Hou Ying's reminder that a general in the field need not accept every order put Zhu Hai at his side with a mallet up his sleeve: if Jin Bi complied, well; if not, strike. The author's inference: the hard part here was not daring. The prince's response on hearing the plan was tears — he said he feared Jin Bi would not obey, and that he would then have to be killed, and that he was not afraid to die. In the author's view, judging by the outcome, he took on a debt to his own side — killing his country's veteran commander, stealing the king's tally, angering the king — and he went through with it anyway. The source records that he foresaw beforehand that Jin Bi might not obey and would then have to be killed; as for the other costs, such as stealing the tally and angering the king, the source does not say whether he weighed them beforehand.
先说史源。本文只依据并核对了《史记·魏公子列传》一篇，未与其他记载对照。文中的对话与献计，如侯嬴献窃符之计、朱亥答话，是史家的记述，未必逐字。公子的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」都是叙述用语，不是实录的心理。纪年照原文写魏安釐王二十年，不换算公元。

Start with the sources. This piece relies on, and was checked against, one chapter only — the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian — without comparison to other accounts. The dialogue and the proposed scheme — Hou Ying's plan to steal the tally, Zhu Hai's reply — are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. The prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame, as the narrative describes them, are narrative labels, not recorded psychology. The year is given as the twentieth of King Anxi of Wei, as the source has it, with no conversion to the common era.
细节上更该存疑的是：「得選兵八萬人」在本篇只出现一次，本文未与其他记载对照；侯生自刭，原文记他此前说过「老臣不能從」，又自言「北鄉自剄，以送公子」，除此之外的动机，本文不作推测。

The detail most worth doubting: the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears only once in this chapter, and this piece has not compared it with other accounts; as for Hou Ying cutting his throat, the source records that he had earlier said this old servant could not follow, and that he himself said he would face north and cut his throat to see the prince off; beyond that, this piece does not speculate about his motives.
本篇只依据并核对了《史记·魏公子列传》一篇，未与他书对照；对话与献计是史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语而非实录心理；不换算公元年份；「得選兵八萬人」在本篇只出现一次。

This piece relies on, and was checked against, one chapter only (the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian), without comparison to other works. The dialogue and the proposed scheme are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim; the prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame are narrative labels rather than recorded psychology; years are not converted to the common era; the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears only once in this chapter.
